description: This entry covers What Topology Studies as part of the fundamentals of topology. In this field, topological spaces matters because sets with a notion of open sets abstracting continuity beyond metrics. It is taught at the Foundations level of the teaching ladder, building from first principles toward professional practice, with each concept defined before it is used.
overview: Topology is the field concerned with The mathematics of shape and continuity: what stays the same when you stretch but never tear. What Topology Studies belongs to its essential core. Concretely: Topological spaces — sets with a notion of open sets abstracting continuity beyond metrics. And Compactness — every open cover has a finite subcover, the abstract source of maxima existing. Mastering this entry means being able to explain the topic in plain sentences, recognize it in real cases, and apply it alongside the neighboring ideas of the Foundations tier.
core_concepts: Topological spaces: sets with a notion of open sets abstracting continuity beyond metrics.
Compactness: every open cover has a finite subcover, the abstract source of maxima existing.
key_laws: Brouwer fixed-point theorem: every continuous map of a disc to itself fixes some point.
vocabulary: Open set: the primitive notion replacing epsilon-balls.
Quotient: gluing a space along an equivalence relation.
methods: Open-set arguments: proving continuity and convergence from the axioms.
